+#
+# Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
+# to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
+# `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
+# line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
+# (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
+# tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
+# one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
+# \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
+# missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
+#   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
+#     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
+#     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
+#     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
+#     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
+#     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
+#     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
+#     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
+#     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
+#     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
+#     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
+#     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
+#     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
+#     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
+#   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
+#     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
+#     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
+#     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
+#     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
+#     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
+#     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,
+#     a leading backslash, quote, paren or brace, assignments, an absolute
+#     path); a segment whose command word is a fence verb (rm git find dd
+#     mkfs* shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP
+#     DELETE TRUNCATE) is kept on its own line for the normal rules, other
+#     segments are dropped. The body falls back to a full scan when it holds
+#     `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(` under an unquoted delimiter, or a segment
+#     word is an interpreter or wrapper, or a variable (`$x -rf /`; such a
+#     segment is ALSO scanned as rm, git and kubectl with the same arguments).
+#     Special case (the #1245 scrub): a standalone quoted-delimiter `cat`
+#     whose header is exactly `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops the whole body.
+#   none — the consumer is on neither list: full scan.
+# Documented gap: a body written to a plain file by one command and executed
+# by a LATER command is outside a per-command fence (the Write tool shares it).
+# =============================================================================
+_bdb_hd_op_re='^[0-9]*(<<<|<<-|&>>|<<|>>|>[|]|&&|[|][|]|[|]&|&>|<>|>&[0-9-]*|<&[0-9-]*|;;|;|&|[|]|<|>|[(]|[)])$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dw='^[A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dsq="^'([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)'\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_ddq='^"([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)"$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dbs='^\\([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_psq="^'([^']*)'\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_pdq="^\"([^\"\$\`\\\\]*)\"\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_pbare="^[^'\"\$\`\\\\]+\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_ctl=$'[\x01-\x08\x0b-\x1f\x7f]'
+_bdb_hd_re_exflag='^-[A-Za-z]*[cex][A-Za-z]*$'
+_bdb_hd_re_exlong='^--(exec|eval|command|in-?place)'
+_bdb_hd_re_ext='\.(sh|bash|zsh|ksh|csh|fish|py|pyw|rb|pl|pm|js|mjs|cjs|ts|mts|cts|ps1|psm1|php|lua|tcl|command|bat|cmd)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_sys='(^|/)(\.claude/hooks(/|$)|\.claude/settings[^/]*\.json$|\.git/hooks(/|$)|\.git/config$|\.gitconfig$|\.ssh/rc$|\.config/(fish|zsh|bash|git)/|s?bin/[^/]+$)'
+_bdb_hd_re_rc='(^|/)\.(bashrc|bash_profile|bash_login|bash_logout|profile|zshrc|zshenv|zprofile|zlogin|zlogout|kshrc|mkshrc|cshrc|tcshrc|login|logout|envrc)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_sedp='^(([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/)(,([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/))?)?p$'
+_bdb_hd_re_assign='^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*='
+_bdb_hd_re_varw='^[$]([{]|[A-Za-z_])'
+_bdb_hd_re_knob='^[[:space:]]+heredoc_classifier:[[:space:]]*["'"'"']?([A-Za-z]+)["'"'"']?[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$'
+
+# Shells, interpreters and wrappers that run their argument or stdin.
+_bdb_hd_is_interp() {
+  case "$1" in
+    bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh|mksh|ash|fish|csh|tcsh|busybox|python|python[0-9]*|pypy*|node|nodejs|deno|bun|ruby|irb|perl|php|lua|luajit|tclsh|wish|expect|pwsh|powershell|osascript|Rscript) return 0 ;;
+    eval|source|.|exec|command|builtin|time|awk|gawk|mawk|nawk|make|gmake|m4|ed|ex|vi|vim|nvim|gdb) return 0 ;;
+    sudo|doas|su|runuser|env|xargs|parallel|timeout|nohup|nice|ionice|setsid|stdbuf|chroot|unshare|nsenter|ssh|docker|podman|kubectl|find|watch|script) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+# The SQL runners of the FR-1.4/5/6 precondition (same list).
+_bdb_hd_is_runner() {
+  case "$1" in
+    psql|pgcli|mysql|mariadb|mysqlsh|sqlite3|sqlcmd|sqlplus|isql|usql|litecli|duckdb|clickhouse|clickhouse-client|cockroach|bq|wrangler|prisma|supabase|drizzle-kit|knex|sequelize|typeorm|flyway|liquibase|dbmate|goose|sqitch|rails|manage.py|artisan|alembic|dbt|atlas|mongosh|sqlx) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+# Command words the fence's own rules match.
+_bdb_hd_is_destructive() {
+  case "$1" in
+    rm|git|find|dd|shred|truncate|kubectl|terraform|aws|gcloud|psql|mysql|mkfs|mkfs.*) return 0 ;;
+    [Dd][Rr][Oo][Pp]|[Dd][Ee][Ll][Ee][Tt][Ee]|[Tt][Rr][Uu][Nn][Cc][Aa][Tt][Ee]) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+# Readers that may name a heredoc's target elsewhere on the line.
+_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader() {
+  case "$1" in
+    cat|ls|wc|head|tail|grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|diff|cmp|stat|file|test|'['|echo|printf|sort|uniq|jq|yq|git|gh|br|mkdir|touch|realpath|readlink|basename|dirname|du|md5sum|sha1sum|sha256sum|shasum|b2sum|cksum) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators
+# are separate tokens, an fd number joins its redirect). Returns 1 when the
+# line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
+_bdb_hd_tokenize() {
+  local s="${1:-}" n i=0 ch tok="" q="" have=0 op cand
+  n=${#s}
+  _bdb_hd_tok=()
+  while (( i < n )); do
+    ch="${s:i:1}"
+    if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
+      tok="$tok$ch"
+      if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
+        [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
+      elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
+        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
+        i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
+      elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then
+        q=""
+      fi
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    case "$ch" in
+      "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '\')
+        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
+      ' '|$'\t')
+        if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
+        i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '#')
+        (( have )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
+        op=""
+        for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
+          if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
+        done
+        i=$((i + ${#op}))
+        if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
+          while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
+        fi
+        if (( have )); then
+          if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
+            op="$tok$op"
+          else
+            _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
+          fi
+          tok=""; have=0
+        fi
+        _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
+      *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+    esac
+  done
+  [[ -z "$q" ]] || return 1
+  (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_unq_path <word> → _hd_up; returns 1 for a non-literal path (an
+# expansion, an escape, mixed quoting) or an empty one.
+_bdb_hd_unq_path() {
+  _hd_up=""
+  if [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq ]] || [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]]; then
+    _hd_up="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
+  elif [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pbare ]]; then
+    _hd_up="$1"
+  else
+    return 1
+  fi
+  [[ -n "$_hd_up" ]]
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_exec_dest <unquoted path> → 0 when a write there is executable
+# content (or cannot be judged).
+_bdb_hd_exec_dest() {
+  local p="${1:-}" d e b old_ifs
+  case "$p" in
+    *'*'*|*'?'*|*'['*|*'{'*|'~'|'~'[!/]*|'') return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  [[ "$p" == '~/'* ]] && p="${HOME:-}/${p#'~/'}"
+  b="${p##*/}"
+  [[ "$b" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ext ]] && return 0
+  [[ "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sys || "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_rc ]] && return 0
+  [[ "$p" == /etc/* ]] && return 0
+  if [[ "$p" == /* ]]; then d="${p%/*}"; [[ -n "$d" ]] || d="/"
+  elif [[ "$p" == */* ]]; then d="${PWD:-.}/${p%/*}"
+  else d="${PWD:-.}"
+  fi
+  old_ifs="$IFS"; IFS=':'
+  for e in ${PATH:-}; do
+    [[ -z "$e" || "$e" == "." ]] && e="${PWD:-.}"
+    [[ "$e" != "/" ]] && e="${e%/}"
+    if [[ "$d" == "$e" ]]; then IFS="$old_ifs"; return 0; fi
+  done
+  IFS="$old_ifs"
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_member <tokens…> → _hd_mcls (interpreter|nonexec|none) for one
+# pipeline member; write targets are appended to _hd_dests.
+_bdb_hd_member() {
+  local -a toks argv
+  local t nxt i n stdout_files=0 a0 base fd stdin=0 ops=0 want="" has_n=0 script=""
+  toks=("$@"); n=${#toks[@]}; argv=()
+  _hd_mcls=none
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    t="${toks[i]}"
+    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then
+      case "$t" in
+        *'<<<') return ;;
+        *'<<'|*'<<-') i=$((i + 1)); continue ;;
+        *'>&'[0-9]*|*'>&-'|*'<&'*) continue ;;
+        *'>'|*'>>'|*'>|'|*'>&'|'&>'|'&>>')
+          nxt="${toks[i+1]:-}"; i=$((i + 1))
+          if [[ -z "$nxt" || "$nxt" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
+          _bdb_hd_unq_path "$nxt" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
+          case "$_hd_up" in /dev/null|/dev/stdout|/dev/stderr) continue ;; esac
+          _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up"
+          fd="${t%%[>&]*}"
+          [[ -z "$fd" || "$fd" == 1 || "$t" == '&>'* || "$t" == '>&' ]] && stdout_files=$((stdout_files + 1))
+          continue ;;
+        *) return ;;
+      esac
+    fi
+    argv[${#argv[@]}]="$t"
+  done
+  (( ${#argv[@]} > 0 )) || return
+  a0="${argv[0]}"
+  base="${a0#\\}"; base="${base##*/}"
+  if _bdb_hd_is_interp "$base" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$base"; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
+  [[ "$a0" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$ ]] || return
+  (( stdout_files <= 1 )) || return
+  for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+    t="${argv[i]}"
+    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exflag || "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exlong ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
+  done
+  case "$a0" in
+    cat)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do [[ "${argv[i]}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; done ;;
+    tee)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -a|--append|-p) ;;
+          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+          *) _bdb_hd_unq_path "$t" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
+             _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up" ;;
+        esac
+      done ;;
+    echo|printf)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        case "${argv[i]}" in -n|-E) ;; -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;; esac
+      done ;;
+    gh)
+      case "${argv[1]:-} ${argv[2]:-}" in
+        "pr comment"|"issue comment") want=" -F --body-file -R --repo |" ;;
+        "pr create") want=" -F --body-file --title -t --base -B --head -H --repo -R --label -l --reviewer -r --assignee -a --milestone -m --project -p --template -T | --draft -d --fill --fill-first --fill-verbose --no-maintainer-edit --dry-run " ;;
+        *) return ;;
+      esac
+      for ((i = 3; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          --body-file=-) stdin=1 ;;
+          --*=*) [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" ${t%%=*} "* ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+          -*)
+            if [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" $t "* ]]; then
+              i=$((i + 1))
+              [[ ( "$t" == "-F" || "$t" == "--body-file" ) && "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1
+            elif [[ "${want#*|}" != *" $t "* ]]; then
+              _hd_mcls=interpreter; return
+            fi ;;
+          *) ops=$((ops + 1)); [[ "${argv[2]}" == comment && $ops -le 1 ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+        esac
+      done
+      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+    git)
+      [[ "${argv[1]:-}" == commit ]] || return
+      for ((i = 2; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -F|--file) i=$((i + 1)); [[ "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; stdin=1 ;;
+          --file=-|-F-) stdin=1 ;;
+          -q|--quiet|-s|--signoff|-a|--all|--allow-empty|--allow-empty-message|-v|--verbose|--no-edit|--amend) ;;
+          *) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+        esac
+      done
+      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+    br)
+      case "${argv[1]:-}" in create|update) ;; *) return ;; esac
+      for ((i = 2; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -d|--description|--body) [[ "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
+          -f|--file) [[ "${argv[1]}" == create && "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
+          --description=-|--body=-) stdin=1 ;;
+        esac
+      done
+      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+    jq|yq)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        # In-place flags: --inplace/--in-place, -i, -i=…, and any short-flag cluster holding an i
+        # (corpus D114/D115: `-i` alone did not match `-[A-Za-z]*i*`, which needs a letter before the i).
+        case "${argv[i]}" in --inplace|--in-place|-i*|-[A-Za-z]*i*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;; esac
+      done ;;
+    grep|egrep|fgrep) ;;
+    sed)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -n|--quiet|--silent) has_n=1 ;;
+          -E|-r|--regexp-extended|-s|--separate|-u|--unbuffered|-z|--null-data) ;;
+          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+          *) if [[ -z "$script" ]]; then
+               script="$t"; [[ "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq || "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]] && script="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
+               [[ "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sedp ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
+             fi ;;
+        esac
+      done
+      (( has_n )) && [[ -n "$script" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+    sort)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -o) i=$((i + 1)); _bdb_hd_unq_path "${argv[i]:-}" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up" ;;
+          -k|-t) i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+          -k*|-t*) ;;
+          --*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+          -*) [[ "$t" =~ ^-[bdfghiMnRrsuVz]+$ ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+        esac
+      done ;;
+    wc)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        case "${argv[i]}" in -*) [[ "${argv[i]}" =~ ^-[lwmL]+$ ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;; esac
+      done ;;
+    *) return ;;
+  esac
+  _hd_mcls=nonexec
+}

+# _bdb_hd_ctx_bad <line> → 0 when a line before (or the header itself) leaves
+# the next text inside a substitution, group, quote, compound command or
+# pipeline: a later heredoc there is interpreter-class.
+_bdb_hd_ctx_bad() {
+  local l="${1:-}" k last
+  case "$l" in *'$('*|*'`'*|*'<('*|*'>('*) return 0 ;; esac
+  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$l" || return 0

+    case "${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}" in
+      '('|')'|'{'|'}'|do|done|then|else|elif|if|fi|while|until|for|case|esac|select|function|coproc) return 0 ;;
+    esac
+  done
+  (( ${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]} > 0 )) || return 1

+# _bdb_hd_header <line> — parse one header line. Sets _hd_ops (heredoc count,

+_bdb_hd_header() {

+  local -a tpipe mtoks

    12	#       `derive --write` (a missing ledger is skipped). Exit 0 · 2 usage /
    13	#       no run · 3 write failed (the previous file is untouched).
    14	#   run-checkpoint.sh read [--file F] [--json]

    19	#       "sprint granularity". Exit 0 always when F exists; 2 when it does not.

   278	   | map(select($reset == null or ((.ts // "") > $reset)))
   279	   | sort_by([(.ts // ""), .round, (if .gate == "review" then 0 else 1 end)])

   281	  | reduce $nr[] as $r ({cycle: 0, same: 0, hash: null, np: 0, lc: null};

   283	      | (if $r.hash != "none" and $r.hash == .hash then .same += 1 else .same = 1 | .hash = $r.hash end)

   285	      | (if .lc != null and .lc == $c then .np += 1 else .np = 0 end)

   287	def skeleton($th; $ts):
   288	  {state: "CLOSED",
   289	   triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: $th.same, last_hash: null},
   290	              no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: $th.np},
   291	              cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: $th.cycles},
   292	              timeout: {started: $ts, limit_hours: $th.hours}},
   293	   history: []};
   294	def merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts):
   295	  (if type == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
   296	  | .triggers = (.triggers // {})
   297	  | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ([(.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0), $rc.cycle] | max)
   298	  | (if $rc.same > (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0)
   299	     then .triggers.same_issue.count = $rc.same | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $rc.hash else . end)
   300	  | (if $rc.np > (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) or (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts == null and $rc.lc != null)
   301	     then .triggers.no_progress.count = ([(.triggers.no_progress.count // 0), $rc.np] | max)
   302	          | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $rc.lc else . end)
   303	  | ( if (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
   304	        then ["same_issue", "same issue hash repeated \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times (derived from the feedback history)"]
   305	      elif (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
   306	        then ["no_progress", "counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
   307	      elif (.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)

   309	      else null end ) as $trip
   310	  | if $trip != null and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
   311	    then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], source: "derive"}])
   312	    else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end;
   313	def known_ids: (.derivation.sprint_ids // null) // ((.sprints.list // []) | map(.id? // empty));
   314	def resolve($f; $now; $win):
   315	  . as $c
   316	  | (if ($c | type) == "object" then $c else {} end) as $c
   317	  | ($c.state // $c.status // "") as $cs
   318	  | ($c | known_ids) as $known
   319	  | ([$f.sprints[] | select(.state != "complete")
   320	      | "sprint-\(.global_id)" as $g | .local_label as $l
   321	      | select(($known | index($g)) == null and ($l == "" or ($known | index($l)) == null))] | length > 0) as $new
   322	  | ((($c.completion // {}) | .merged_sha? // "") | type == "string" and length > 0) as $merged
   323	  | if ($c.state // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or ($c.status // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or $merged then "JACKED_OUT"
   324	    elif $f.breaker_open or $cs == "HALTED" then "HALTED"
   325	    elif $f.all_complete then "COMPLETE"
   326	    elif $cs == "COMPLETE" and ($new | not) then "COMPLETE"
   327	    elif ($c.timestamps.last_activity? // null) | fresh($now; $win) then "RUNNING"
   328	    else "INTERRUPTED" end;
   329	'

+### Heredoc consumer classification (cycle-129 FR-6)
+
+Knob: `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier` (default `true`; `false` restores the pre-cycle scan and is the rollback key). The fence reads the knob from `.loa.config.yaml` only for commands that hold `<<`. The full grammar, both class lists and the default are stated in the block comment above `_bdb_hd_is_interp` in `block-destructive-bash.sh`. In summary:
+
+- **Grammar.** The fence sees literal command text, with CRLF folded to LF. A control character, an unreadable header, more than one heredoc on a header, a non-word or variable delimiter, or a missing terminator makes the whole command scan in full.
+- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. This applies when the consumer or any pipe target is a shell, interpreter, argument-running wrapper or SQL runner, when the statement holds a substitution, group or continuation, or when an allowlisted form carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag. It also applies when the write target is executable content: a script extension, a shebang first line, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.git/hooks/`, an rc or profile file, `/etc`, or a directory on `PATH`. Naming the target elsewhere on the same command outside a safe reader has the same effect.
+- **Non-executing class.** This covers exact forms only: `cat`, `tee`, `printf` and `echo` to a plain file or stdout, `gh pr|issue comment -F -`, `gh pr create --body-file -`, `git commit -F -`, `br create|update` reading stdin, `jq`/`yq` without in-place, `grep`, print-only `sed -n`, `sort` and `wc`. Their bodies are scanned per segment. Segments that start with a fence verb are kept for the normal rules, and the rest are dropped. A substitution under an unquoted delimiter, an interpreter word or a variable command word sends the body back to a full scan.
+- **Default.** A consumer on neither list, or a parse failure, scans in full. The #1245 quoted standalone `cat` scrub is the special case and is also the knob-off path.
+- **Export.** Source the hook with `BDB_LIB_ONLY=1` and call `_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command>`, which prints `interpreter`, `nonexec` or `none`. `heredoc_nonexec <command>` exits 0 for a non-executing heredoc. Library mode applies only when the file is sourced. An executed hook ignores the variable.
+- **Remaining gap.** A body written to a plain file by one command and executed by a later command is outside a per-command fence. The Write tool shares this limit.

One residual false positive is **accepted by design**:

The `$(` disqualifies the value from redaction (a regex fence cannot parse subshell contents without reintroducing the #1047 bypass), so a destructive *shape* mentioned inside that subshell body still trips FR-2 and blocks a genuinely safe commit. **Workaround**: paraphrase the destructive shape in the commit body (as the cycle-119 commits did — e.g. write "find-exec-rm" rather than the literal `find … -exec rm -rf`), or drop the `$(…)` wrapper. content.content:
DISS-C-001 [HIGH] .claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:check_implement_marker
  
  The new `sanctioned_marker` path grants an unconditional allow (even under `implement_gate.mode: deny`) whenever `.run/implement-active.json` holds `{skill: implement|bug, sprint: <token>, started_at: <2h}`. That file is model-authored: the model can run `run-checkpoint.sh mark` or simply `printf '{"skill":"implement","sprint":"x","started_at":"'$(date -u +%FT%TZ)'"}' > .run/implement-active.json` from the Bash tool. The hook only guards Write/Edit, so the trust-input ask on `.run/implement-active.json` (line 340) does not cover Bash writes. The same file's own header comment treats the model-authored `tool_input.active_skill` claim as tighten-only precisely because it is model-authored; the marker is the same trust class but is allowed to grant. Likewise, a Bash `rm .run/sprint-plan-state.json` degrades deny to ask (`unknown_position`).

DISS-C-002 [MEDIUM] .claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:590
  
  `LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=1` in the hook's environment sanctions every App Zone write in every mode including deny. block-destructive-bash.sh (same PR) explicitly states the opposite principle for its fence: 'an environment variable can never switch the fence off'. Hook environment can be influenced by repo-controlled files loaded before Claude Code starts (direnv `.envrc`, shell rc files, `.claude/settings*.json` `env` blocks), several of which the heredoc classifier itself treats as executable content.

DISS-C-003 [MEDIUM] .claude/data/profiles.yaml:standard
  
  Two security guardrails flip from default-on to default-off. `is_enforcement_enabled()` previously returned true when the key was unset and when `.loa.config.yaml` was absent; it now returns `loa_knob guardrails.danger_level.enforce false`, which resolves to `false` under the default `standard` profile (and `lean`). `input_guardrails.md` previously ran unless explicitly disabled; it now runs only if the knob prints `true`, which `standard` does not. In addition, `source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/profile-lib.sh"` is unconditional with no error handling: if the lib is missing or `loa_knob` fails, `enforce` is empty and enforcement is off (fail-open).

DISS-C-004 [MEDIUM] .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:_bdb_hd_same_line_exec
  
  The classifier decides a heredoc body is 'nonexec' and drops non-fence-verb segments when the write target is not detected as executed in the same command. `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` requires the target's literal basename to appear as a token after quote-stripping; a glob (`bash t*`, `. ./pay?oad`), brace expansion, or `${var}` built path (`bash "${PWD}/${n}"`) that resolves to the file is not matched, so the body is still scrubbed. `_bdb_hd_exec_dest` resolves relative targets against the hook process's `$PWD`, ignoring a `cd /usr/local/bin &&` in the same command, so a write into a PATH or bin directory is judged non-executable. Line numbers are approximate; the symbol anchor is authoritative.

DISS-C-005 [MEDIUM] .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:_bdb_hd_is_destructive
  
  Under the default `heredoc_classifier: true`, a 'nonexec' heredoc body is reduced to only those segments whose command word is in this hardcoded list (rm git find dd shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql mkfs* DROP DELETE TRUNCATE). The main fence's rule set is maintained separately (`_bdb_re_git`, `_bdb_re_brbd`, and the rest of the file not shown); any rule keyed on a verb absent here (e.g. `br`/`bd` delete, `gh repo delete`, `chmod`, `chown`, `mv`, `crontab -r`, device redirects, fork bomb) is silently excluded from heredoc bodies. The quote-stripping in `_bdb_hd_segword` also yields `r` for `'r'm -rf /`, so a trivially quoted verb is dropped before the fence rules ever see it. Nothing ties this allow-list to the rule set, so future rule additions will not propagate.

DISS-C-006 [MEDIUM] .claude/data/constraints.json:C-TEAM-005
  
  All five agent-team constraints are removed, including C-TEAM-005 (teammates MUST NOT modify `.claude/`, 'enforced by PreToolUse:Write/Edit hook', severity critical, incident bridgebuilder-horizon-pr341) and C-TEAM-002/003/004 (lead-only beads, .run state, and git commit/push). The constraint text was the prompt-layer control that told teammates not to rewrite hooks, constraints, or settings for every agent in a team. No replacement constraint appears in the diff, and the implement-gate rows show `LOA_TEAM_MEMBER` is still a live role, so teammates still exist.

DISS-C-007 [LOW] .claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:read_position
  
  `position_state` is taken from `.state // .status` of `.run/sprint-plan-state.json`, control-stripped but not length-limited, then interpolated into the stderr line and the `permissionDecisionReason` JSON returned to the harness via `deny_reason`. Every other untrusted string this hook emits (file_path, active_skill) is cut to 256 bytes per the sprint-250 audit notes; this new one is not.

# Sprint 1 Security Audit Feedback

**Auditor:** Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor
**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (pr/PR.md)
**Change under audit:** pr/head.diff — cycle-129 sprint-256 (68 files, +4,665 / −1,281 lines)

---

## Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

---

## Executive Summary

The sprint adds four controls to the framework's safety surface: a heredoc consumer classifier inside the Bash fence, a `deny` mode for the implement gate backed by a file-derived run position, a profile layer (`loa.profile` + `profile-lib.sh`) that now sits in front of both guardrail switches, and a derived circuit breaker. Every new state file is written atomically, model-authored strings reaching stderr or audit rows are control-stripped and cut to 256 bytes, every key path reaching a yq expression is regex-checked, and the fence's library mode cannot be switched on from the environment of an executed hook. The corpus (231 rows) decides as declared on this host.

Three defects block the merge. Two are toolchain-portability bugs that make the PR's own controls inert on the documented jq floor: `run-checkpoint.sh derive` cannot compile on jq 1.6 (so the `deny` gate never has a known position) and `fb_parse`'s empty-input guards do not fire on jq 1.6 (so the breaker aborts on any legacy feedback file). The third is a fence regression: the classifier judges write destinations and same-command executors by literal text, so a `..` or `//` segment in a `.git/hooks` path, or a backslash-escaped filename on the executing line, turns a body the base fence blocked into a "non-executing" body whose keyword-prefixed lines are dropped. All three were reproduced independently (the first two on this host; the third by the senior review's base-vs-head replay and, with a new variant, by the cross-model dissenter's primary voice).

Below the blockers, one new finding of this audit: the profile cache `.run/effective-config.json` is read in preference to `.loa.config.yaml` whenever its id matches, is not in the implement gate's trust-input list, and so lets a silent State-Zone write override an explicit `guardrails.*: true` that a config edit would have had to ask for.

**Prerequisite deviation.** Phase 0 requires `engineer-feedback.md` to say "All good"; it says CHANGES REQUIRED (3 high). The task brief for this evaluation instructs the audit to run regardless and to write this file, so the audit proceeded. The review's blockers are re-examined below as findings of this audit, not inherited.

**Security Issues Found:**

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 3 |
| Medium | 8 |
| Low | 8 |

---

## Critical Security Issues (Must Fix)

None.

---

## High Priority Security Issues (Fix Before Deployment)

### [HIGH-001] `derive` does not compile on the documented jq floor, so `deny` mode never engages

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378` (binding), `:380` and `:389` (uses)
**Issue:** The per-sprint jq program is invoked with `--arg label "$label"` and reads `$label`. `label` is a jq keyword; jq 1.6 rejects it: `syntax error, unexpected label, expecting IDENT or __loc__`. Reproduced on this host (jq-1.6) by running `derive --json --root /workspace` against this repository's ledger: two compile errors, no report. `tests/unit/run-checkpoint-derive.bats` fails 18 of 22 cases here for this reason alone. `.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh` documents the floor as "install jq 1.6+".
**Impact:** `derive`, `derive --write`, and the derive step that `write` and `mark` run at every checkpoint all fail, so `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` never gains `derived_at`. `implement-gate.sh read_position` (`head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:558`) then always returns "cache not derived", and `implement_gate.mode: deny` degrades to ask on every write. The control the PR introduces as "a fence only in this mode" is inert on Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04 hosts, silently.
**PoC:**
```
$ jq --version
jq-1.6
$ bash .claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh derive --json --root /workspace
jq: error: syntax error, unexpected label, expecting IDENT or __loc__ ... line 2:
      def mine: ... ($label != "" and . == $label));
jq: 2 compile errors
```
**Fix:** Rename the binding (`--arg lbl "$label"` / `$lbl`); grep every jq program added in this PR for keyword-named variables; add jq 1.6 to CI or raise the documented floor to 1.7 in `dec-write-lib.sh` and the install docs. Do not leave the floor and the code disagreeing.
**Reference:** CWE-754 Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html; jq 1.6 manual, `label $name`.

### [HIGH-002] `fb_parse`'s empty-input guards never fire on jq 1.6; the breaker aborts on legacy feedback

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:223` and `:226`
**Issue:** `jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='…'` assumes `jq -e` exits non-zero on empty input. On jq 1.6 it exits 0 (reproduced: `printf '' | jq -e 'type=="object"'; echo $?` → 0; jq 1.7 returns 4). An empty `$pj` — every feedback file without a `LOA-VERDICT` trailer, the legacy class the PR explicitly supports via `derivation.legacy_feedback` — then reaches `--argjson`, which aborts (`invalid JSON text passed to --argjson`, reproduced), and `set -euo pipefail` (line 78) kills the script. `tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats` RCR-7 fails here for this reason.
**Impact:** `record-round` exits 2 and records nothing for a trailer-less review or audit file, and `derive` aborts for any sprint carrying one. The run-mode SKILL (`head/.claude/skills/run-mode/SKILL.md`, the record-round step) treats exit 10 as the halt signal; an exit 2 is neither "recorded" nor "halted", so the circuit breaker silently stops counting in exactly the legacy case the no-trailer hash was written for.
**Fix:** Test the string before calling jq (`{ [[ -n "$vj" ]] && jq -e … <<<"$vj"; } || vj=…`, same for `$pj`), audit every `jq -e … <<<"$x" || default` idiom added in this PR, and add a jq-1.6 legacy-feedback case to the derive suite.
**Reference:** CWE-754 — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html; CWE-390 Detection of Error Condition Without Action — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/390.html.

### [HIGH-003] Fence: executable-destination and same-command-executor checks compare literal text, and keyword-prefixed body segments are dropped

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:303` (`_bdb_hd_exec_dest`), `:190` (`_bdb_hd_re_sys`), `:608` (`_bdb_hd_same_line_exec`), `:576`–`:600` (`_bdb_hd_scan_body`)
**Issue:** Three literal-text comparisons combine into a regression versus the base fence for the one class the PR says it fails closed on ("a write target is executable content").
- `_bdb_hd_exec_dest` tests the un-normalised path against `_bdb_hd_re_sys`, so `.git/objects/../hooks/pre-commit`, `.git//hooks/pre-commit` and `.git/./hooks/pre-commit` do not match `\.git/hooks(/|$)` and classify as plain files. The same applies to `.claude/./hooks/<name>` without an extension, and to `.git/modules/<sub>/hooks/<name>` (submodule hooks), which the regex never covered.
- `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` strips quotes and the directory from each token and tests equality with the target's basename; a backslash-escaped name (`bash /tmp/pay\load`, which bash resolves to `payload`), a `$(cat <target>)` substitution on a later line, a glob (`bash t*`), or a `${var}`-built path never match, so the body

The PR rebuilds three safety controls at once: the Bash fence's heredoc handling, the implement gate's modes and sanctions, and the run position plus circuit breaker derived from files. It also routes nine optional surfaces, including both guardrails, through a new profile resolver. The direction is sound, and the gate's mode matrix and the profile floor are carefully built. But four defects block the merge.

- **The run-position work is dead on the declared jq floor.** `derive` cannot compile on jq 1.6 and `record-round` aborts on any feedback file without a trailer, so `deny` mode is inert and the breaker stops counting.

## High Priority Security Issues (Fix Before Deployment)

### [HIGH-001] `derive` cannot compile on jq 1.6, so the file-authoritative run position never exists

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378`
**Issue:** The per-sprint jq program binds a variable named after a jq keyword:

```
sj=$(jq -nc --argjson gid "$gid" --arg label "$label" ...
```

jq 1.6 rejects `$label` at compile time. Reproduced against this repository's own ledger:

```
jq: error: syntax error, unexpected label, expecting IDENT or __loc__ ...
      {global_id: $gid, local_label: $label, status: $status,
jq: 2 compile errors
```

`derive`, `derive --write`, and the derive step that `write` and `mark` run at every checkpoint all fail. `cmd_write` swallows the error, so the cache never gains `derived_at`.
**Impact:** The implement gate's `read_position` requires a fresh `derived_at`. Without one, `implement_gate.mode: deny` always falls back to ask, so the PR's new fence never engages. The `/loa` drift line never prints. 18 of 22 derive tests fail on this host. The repository's own documented floor is jq 1.6+, so this is a supported host, not an exotic one.
**Fix:** Rename the binding, for example `--arg lbl "$label"` and `$lbl` in the program. Check the other new jq programs for keyword-named variables. Add jq 1.6 to CI or raise the documented floor everywhere it is stated.
**Reference:** CWE-758, Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior, https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/758.html

### [HIGH-002] `fb_parse` empty-input guards never fire on jq 1.6, so the circuit breaker stops counting on legacy feedback

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:223` and `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:226`
**Issue:** Both guards rely on `jq -e` failing on empty input:

```
jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
```

On jq 1.6 an empty input exits 0, verified on this host. An empty `$pj`, which every trailer-less feedback file produces, then reaches `--argjson` and aborts under `set -e` with `invalid JSON text passed to --argjson`.
**Impact:** `record-round` exits 2 on a legacy feedback file and records nothing. The run-mode skill only treats exit 10 as a trip, so the breaker silently stops counting in exactly the legacy case the no-trailer hash was written for. A runaway review loop is then bounded only by the cycle count it can no longer see. RCR-7 fails on this host for this reason.
**Fix:** Test the string before calling jq, for example `{ [[ -n "$pj" ]] && jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<"$pj"; } >/dev/null 2>&1 || pj='{}'`, and the same for `$vj`. Add a legacy-feedback case that runs under jq 1.6.
**Reference:** CWE-754, Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions, https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html

### [HIGH-003] Heredoc classifier: destinations are judged before canonicalisation, and keyword-prefixed body segments are dropped

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high; confirmed by the senior review's base-versus-head reproduction and by cross-model dissent)
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:303`, with the pattern at `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:190` and the body scan at `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:576`
**Issue:** `_bdb_hd_exec_dest` matches the literal target text against `_bdb_hd_re_sys`:

```
[[ "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sys || "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_rc ]] && return 0
```

A path that reaches `.git/hooks/` through a `..` segment or a doubled slash does not match, so it is classed as a plain file. Separately, `_bdb_hd_scan_body` keeps a segment only when its command word is a fence verb. A segment whose word is a shell keyword such as `then` or `do` is dropped, along with the verb that follows it.
**Impact:** Together, the two defects let a hook body containing a destructive command reach `.git/hooks/` with no scan. The base fence blocked the same command and the head fence allows it. The PR title promises a "fail-closed" classifier, and this is the class it claims to close.
**Fix:**
1. Canonicalise the destination lexically before the regex: collapse `//`, drop `./`, resolve `..`. Treat any path that still holds `..` as "cannot be judged" and return 0.
2. In `_bdb_hd_scan_body`, when a segment's word is a shell keyword (`if then else elif fi for while until do done case esac function time ! {`), re-run `_bdb_hd_segword` on the rest instead of dropping it.
3. Add corpus rows for both shapes.

**Reference:** CWE-180, Incorrect Behavior Order: Validate Before Canonicalize, https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/180.html

### [HIGH-004] Heredoc classifier: the same-command executor check compares raw tokens, not resolved shell words

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: medium; raised by the cross-model dissent as DISS-001 at confidence 0.97 and by the senior review as Observation §1; derived here from the code, not re-probed)
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608`
**Issue:** `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` decides whether a plain-file target is executed later in the same command. It strips quotes and the directory from each token and tests string equality with the target's basename:

```
u="${_bdb_hd_tok[c]}"; u="${u//[\"\']/}"; u="${u##*/}"
[[ "$u" == "$b" ]] && seg_has=1
```

Backslash escapes, globs, brace expansion, parameter expansion and command substitution are not resolved. An executor token that bash resolves to the target therefore does not match. The heredoc stays `nonexec`, and with HIGH-003's keyword drop its body is never scanned.
**Impact:** Write a body to a harmless-looking file and run it later in the same Bash call, and the fence will not see it. The PR's header says a later command in the same call is covered. It is not, for any executor word that is not spelled literally. The base fence scanned the whole command and blocked it.
**Fix:** Fail closed. If any token on another line contains a backslash, a glob character, `$`, a backtick or `<(`, and that line is not a safe reader, treat the heredoc as interpreter class. Do not try to emulate word expansion. Use a substring test on the basename rather than equality as a second net.
**Reference:** CWE-184, Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs, https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/184.html

## Medium/Low Priority Issues

### [MED-001] Body-segment verb extraction truncates at a quote, and the verb list is not tied to the rule set

- **Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: medium; dissent DISS-C-005)
- **File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:565`, list at `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:214`
- **Issue:** `_bdb_hd_segword` cuts the command word at its first quote character (`w="${w%%[\"\']*}"`). A verb with an embedded quote is reduced to a fragment, matches no fence verb, and its segment is dropped. `_bdb_hd_is_destructive` is also a hand-kept list. A fence rule keyed on a verb outside that list, now or in the future, never sees a non-executing heredoc body.
- **Fix:** Remove all quote characters from the word rather than truncating. If any quote remains inside the word, keep the segment. Derive the verb list from the rules, or add a lint that fails when a rule's verb is missing from it.
- **Reference:** CWE-184, https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/184.html

- **Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: high; dissent DISS-C-001 rated HIGH)

## High Priority Security Issues (Fix Before Deployment)

### [HIGH-001] `derive` cannot compile on jq 1.6, so the file-authoritative run position never exists

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378`
**Issue:** The per-sprint jq program binds a variable named after a jq keyword:

```
sj=$(jq -nc --argjson gid "$gid" --arg label "$label" ...
```

jq 1.6 rejects `$label` at compile time. Reproduced against this repository's own ledger:

```
jq: error: syntax error, unexpected label, expecting IDENT or __loc__ ...
      {global_id: $gid, local_label: $label, status: $status,
jq: 2 compile errors
```

`derive`, `derive --write`, and the derive step that `write` and `mark` run at every checkpoint all fail. `cmd_write` swallows the error, so the cache never gains `derived_at`.
**Impact:** The implement gate's `read_position` requires a fresh `derived_at`. Without one, `implement_gate.mode: deny` always falls back to ask, so the PR's new fence never engages. The `/loa` drift line never prints. 18 of 22 derive tests fail on this host. The repository's own documented floor is jq 1.6+, so this is a supported host, not an exotic one.
**Fix:** Rename the binding, for example `--arg lbl "$label"` and `$lbl` in the program. Check the other new jq programs for keyword-named variables. Add jq 1.6 to CI or raise the documented floor everywhere it is stated.
**Reference:** CWE-758, Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior, https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/758.html

### [HIGH-002] `fb_parse` empty-input guards never fire on jq 1.6, so the circuit breaker stops counting on legacy feedback

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:223` and `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:226`
**Issue:** Both guards rely on `jq -e` failing on empty input:

```
jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
```

On jq 1.6 an empty input exits 0, verified on this host. An empty `$pj`, which every trailer-less feedback file produces, then reaches `--argjson` and aborts under `set -e` with `invalid JSON text passed to --argjson`.
**Impact:** `record-round` exits 2 on a legacy feedback file and records nothing. The run-mode skill only treats exit 10 as a trip, so the breaker silently stops counting in exactly the legacy case the no-trailer hash was written for. A runaway review loop is then bounded only by the cycle count it can no longer see. RCR-7 fails on this host for this reason.
**Fix:** Test the string before calling jq, for example `{ [[ -n "$pj" ]] && jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<"$pj"; } >/dev/null 2>&1 || pj='{}'`, and the same for `$vj`. Add a legacy-feedback case that runs under jq 1.6.
**Reference:** CWE-754, Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions, https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html

### [HIGH-003] Heredoc classifier: destinations are judged before canonicalisation, and keyword-prefixed body segments are dropped

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high; confirmed by the senior review's base-versus-head reproduction and by cross-model dissent)
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:303`, with the pattern at `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:190` and the body scan at `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:576`
**Issue:** `_bdb_hd_exec_dest` matches the literal target text against `_bdb_hd_re_sys`:

```
[[ "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sys || "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_rc ]] && return 0
```

A path that reaches `.git/hooks/` through a `..` segment or a doubled slash does not match, so it is classed as a plain file. Separately, `_bdb_hd_scan_body` keeps a segment only when its command word is a fence verb. A segment whose word is a shell keyword such as `then` or `do` is dropped, along with the verb that follows it.
**Impact:** Together, the two defects let a hook body containing a destructive command reach `.git/hooks/` with no scan. The base fence blocked the same command and the head fence allows it. The PR title promises a "fail-closed" classifier, and this is the class it claims to close.
**Fix:**
1. Canonicalise the destination lexically before the regex: collapse `//`, drop `./`, resolve `..`. Treat any path that still holds `..` as "cannot be judged" and return 0.
2. In `_bdb_hd_scan_body`, when a segment's word is a shell keyword (`if then else elif fi for while until do done case esac function time ! {`), re-run `_bdb_hd_segword` on the rest instead of dropping it.
3. Add corpus rows for both shapes.

**Reference:** CWE-180, Incorrect Behavior Order: Validate Before Canonicalize, https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/180.html

### [HIGH-004] Heredoc classifier: the same-command executor check compares raw tokens, not resolved shell words

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: medium; raised by the cross-model dissent as DISS-001 at confidence 0.97 and by the senior review as Observation §1; derived here from the code, not re-probed)
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608`
**Issue:** `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` decides whether a plain-file target is executed later in the same command. It strips quotes and the directory from each token and tests string equality with the target's basename:

```
u="${_bdb_hd_tok[c]}"; u="${u//[\"\']/}"; u="${u##*/}"
[[ "$u" == "$b" ]] && seg_has=1
```

Backslash escapes, globs, brace expansion, parameter expansion and command substitution are not resolved. An executor token that bash resolves to the target therefore does not match. The heredoc stays `nonexec`, and with HIGH-003's keyword drop its body is never scanned.
**Impact:** Write a body to a harmless-looking file and run it later in the same Bash call, and the fence will not see it. The PR's header says a later command in the same call is covered. It is not, for any executor word that is not spelled literally. The base fence scanned the whole command and blocked it.
**Fix:** Fail closed. If any token on another line contains a backslash, a glob character, `$`, a backtick or `<(`, and that line is not a safe reader, treat the heredoc as interpreter class. Do not try to emulate word expansion. Use a substring test on the basename rather than equality as a second net.
**Reference:** CWE-184, Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs, https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/184.html

## Medium/Low Priority Issues

### [MED-001] Body-segment verb extraction truncates at a quote, and the verb list is not tied to the rule set

- **Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: medium; dissent DISS-C-005)
- **File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:565`, list at `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:214`
- **Issue:** `_bdb_hd_segword` cuts the command word at its first quote character (`w="${w%%[\"\']*}"`). A verb with an embedded quote is reduced to a fragment, matches no fence verb, and its segment is dropped. `_bdb_hd_is_destructive` is also a hand-kept list. A fence rule keyed on a verb outside that list, now or in the future, never sees a non-executing heredoc body.
- **Fix:** Remove all quote characters from the word rather than truncating. If any quote remains inside the word, keep the segment. Derive the verb list from the rules, or add a lint that fails when a rule's verb is missing from it.
- **Reference:** CWE-184, https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/184.html

### [MED-002] The rc/profile destination list omits files that the shell or ssh execute

- **Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: high; senior review Observation §2, reproduced there against base)
- **File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:191`
- **Issue:** `_bdb_hd_re_rc` omits `.bash_aliases`, which the default Debian and Ubuntu `.bashrc` sources, and `.ssh/config`, whose `ProxyCommand` runs a shell. Appends there are classed plain and allowed. The base fence blocked them.
- **Fix:** Add `bash_aliases`, `zsh_aliases`, `ssh/config`, editor rc files and build recipe files (`Makefile`, `Justfile`) to the executable-destination patterns.
- **Reference:** CWE-184, https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/184.html

### [MED-003] Guardrail readers fail open when the profile resolver cannot run

- **Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: high; reproduced)
- **File:** `head/.claude/scripts/danger-level-enforcer.sh:141`, fallback path at `head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:215`
- **Issue:** `enforce=$(loa_knob guardrails.danger_level.enforce false)` returns the caller's fallback whenever yq is missing or the config does not parse, even if the operator wrote `enforce: true`. Reproduced with a config holding `enforce: true` and yq off `PATH`: the knob printed `false`. The base read defaulted to `true` in that case. The input-guardrail include at `head/.claude/data/skill-includes/input_guardrails.md:3` has the same shape.
- **Fix:** Make `loa_knob` return a distinct status for "unresolvable". Have safety readers default on in that case, or fall back to a direct read of the explicit key.
- **Reference:** CWE-636, Not Failing Securely, https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/636.html

### [MED-004] The profile cache in `.run/` overrides an explicit config value and is not a protected input

- **Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: medium; reproduced)
- **File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:227`, cache path at `head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:67`
- **Issue:** The warm path answers `loa_knob` from `.run/effective-config.json` whenever the cache's `id` matches. The `id` is built from file paths, mtimes and sizes, which a writer can copy. I edited only the knob value in the cache. `guardrails.input.enabled` then read `false` although the config says `true`. The implement gate protects `.loa.config.yaml` as a trust input, but not this file.
- **Impact:** Any Bash command can silently switch off the input guardrails, danger-level enforcement, the surgical-diff warning or the retrospective. The config file stays untouched. This is the same `.run/` trust class as bead bd-taee, but it now reaches every profile key.
- **Fix:** Bind the cache id to a content hash of the three inputs, not mtime and size. Add the cache to the gate's trust-input list. Have safety readers re-read the explicit key live.
- **Reference:** CWE-807, Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision, https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/807.html

### [MED-005] The marker sanction is forgeable from Bash and grants allow under `deny`

- **Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: high; dissent DISS-C-001 rated HIGH)
- **File:** `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:545`
- **Issue:** `check_implement_marker` sanctions any App-Zone write while `.run/implement-active.json` names `implement` or `bug` and is under two hours old. The file is written from Bash, which the gate does not see, so a model can sanction itself. The hook header treats `tool_input.active_skill` as tighten-only because it is model-authored. The marker is the same trust class but is allowed to grant.
- **Why not HIGH:** the hooks reference states this gap, and Bash can already write App-Zone files directly. Forging the marker adds nothing an agent could not already do through Bash. It does mean `deny` is not the boundary the example config's "a fence only in this mode" suggests.
- **Fix:** State in the example config that `deny` is a mistake-catcher for Write/Edit, not a boundary. Consider binding the marker to the session id from the hook payload.
- **Reference:** CWE-807, https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/807.html

### [MED-006] The derived breaker does not reset on approval, and HALTED outranks COMPLETE

- **Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: high; senior review Observation §3, confirmed from the code)
- **File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:280`, ordering at `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:324`
- **Issue:** `recompute` filters out approved rounds before counting streaks (`map(select(.approved | not))`), so an approval never breaks a same-issue streak. A breaker reset made before this PR carries no `reset_at` and filters nothing. `resolve` then ranks `breaker_open` above `all_complete`. Once HIGH-001 is fixed, an upgraded in-flight run can be halted at its next checkpoint, and a finished cycle can report HALTED.
- **Fix:** Count streaks over the full ordered list and reset on an approved round. Treat a zeroed breaker without `reset_at` as reset at the newest round. Rank a derived COMPLETE above a derived OPEN.
- **Reference:** CWE-670, Always-Incorrect Control Flow Implementation, https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/670.html

### [MED-007] The two-hour implement marker is never refreshed

- **Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: high; senior review Observation §4)
- **File:** `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:550`
- **Issue:** `_ig_within 7200 "$started"` bounds the marker. The implementing skills call `mark` once at the start and `unmark` at the end, and nothing refreshes it. Under `deny`, a direct `/implement` that runs past two hours is denied on every App-Zone write. Under `ask`, it prompts on every write.
- **Fix:** Re-run `mark` at each task boundary, or tie the window to `run_mode.stale_hours`. Log a `stale_marker` reason that names the remedy.
- **Reference:** CWE-613, Insufficient Session Expiration (here: a lifetime not tied to activity), https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/613.html

### [MED-008] The surgical-diff hook and the checkpoint write are an order of magnitude slower

- **Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: medium; senior review Observation §5)
- **File:** `head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:131`
- **Issue:** Every Write/Edit now sources the profile resolver, does two knob reads, and spawns `run-checkpoint.sh read --json`. That spawn runs several jq calls and a `br show`. The review measured about 270 to 380 ms per edit against 32 ms on base. Each `run-checkpoint.sh write` now runs a full `derive`.
- **Fix:** Have `write` and `mark` drop the task key in a small file the hook reads directly. Read both knobs in one pass. Derive only on `mark`, `record-round` and phase changes.
